key_insight: PANDA is an unsupervised MRI anomaly detector that learns normal pelvic anatomy from healthy scans and highlights suspicious deviations in real time without needing labeled adverse-event data.
clinical_relevance: It could help radiologists spot unexpected pelvic abnormalities during MRI and adjust scanning or intervention protocols on the spot.
method: Frozen DINOv3 Vision Transformer encoder learns normative pelvic MRI features from healthy cases
Noisy MLP bottleneck plus Linear Attention decoder reduces identity copying while staying efficient
Per-token cosine distance between encoder and decoder outputs generates localized anomaly maps and frame-level scores
evidence_signal: On a curated subset of the Uterine Myoma Dataset, the model achieved 88.06% pixel-level AUROC and 95.45% frame-level specificity while processing 40.5 slices per second.
watch_item: Performance is reported on a curated dataset subset, so broader validation is still needed before real-world deployment across scanners, protocols, and rare anomaly types.
paper_title: Panda: Unsupervised Pelvic Anomaly Detection for Real-Time MR Imaging
